{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Preserve backward compatibility by making all new configuration options optional and retaining existing defaults.",
    "Implement explicit partition count as a source or stream configuration property, with validation against Kafka topic partition availability and clear startup errors.",
    "Implement dynamic Kafka partition subscription using consumer assignment or subscription APIs so partition membership can change without requiring application redeployment.",
    "Implement HDFS Syncable writes as an opt-in sink mode, invoking the appropriate filesystem synchronization operation and documenting its performance implications.",
    "Implement the HDFS in-use suffix behavior as a configurable option; retain the existing temporary suffix as the default and allow an empty suffix to write directly to the configured filename.",
    "Expose custom-module installation through Maven and Gradle tasks that invoke the existing module upload/install mechanism rather than duplicating repository logic.",
    "Version custom modules using explicit module coordinates and version metadata, while retaining compatibility with existing unversioned module references.",
    "Treat PHD 3.0 certification as a compatibility and integration-validation task covering supported Java, Hadoop, HDFS, Kafka, and deployment combinations.",
    "Use automated unit, integration, regression, and command-line/UI-level tests where the existing project test infrastructure supports them."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The increment is implemented in an existing Spring XD codebase with established build, test, module, Kafka, HDFS, and admin UI infrastructure.",
    "The developer has access to the source repository, CI environment, Kafka and HDFS test environments, and a PHD 3.0 environment or equivalent certified distribution.",
    "The reported admin UI job-creation failure is a defect in existing application behavior rather than a missing product capability, and no major redesign of authentication or authorization is required.",
    "The exact desired routing semantics for explicit partition count are limited to configuring and validating the partition-related behavior; a new routing algorithm is not required.",
    "Dynamic partition subscription does not require guaranteed exactly-once processing beyond the guarantees already provided by the existing Kafka source implementation.",
    "HDFS Syncable support can be implemented using APIs available in the currently supported Hadoop dependency set.",
    "Custom-module Maven and Gradle support means adding build targets and associated documentation, not creating new Maven or Gradle plugins.",
    "Custom-module versioning applies to module packaging, registration, lookup, and deployment compatibility, without requiring a new enterprise artifact repository.",
    "PHD 3.0 certification will identify and fix compatibility issues found in the supported test scenarios, but does not include certification of every Spring XD feature or deployment topology.",
    "One workday represents one developer day of focused effort; elapsed calendar time, waiting for environments, and work by additional personnel are excluded.",
    "Documentation and release notes are limited to the new configuration properties, commands, compatibility constraints, and upgrade guidance."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Increment planning and codebase analysis",
      "activity_description": "Review the existing architecture, configuration model, Kafka source, HDFS sink, custom-module lifecycle, admin UI job-creation flow, build scripts, test conventions, and PHD compatibility constraints. Produce an implementation plan and identify affected components.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Investigate and fix admin UI job-creation failure",
      "activity_description": "Reproduce the ROLE_CREATE and ROLE_ADMIN failures, trace the request through the admin UI, server, authorization, validation, and job deployment layers, implement the defect fix, improve error reporting where needed, and add regression coverage.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Implement explicit partition count configuration",
      "activity_description": "Add configuration properties and validation for explicit partition counts, propagate the value through stream or module configuration, implement the required routing behavior, handle invalid and incompatible values, and add unit and integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Implement dynamic Kafka partition subscription",
      "activity_description": "Modify the Kafka source consumer lifecycle to support dynamic partition subscription and reassignment, preserve offsets and existing consumer behavior, handle partition changes and failures, and add tests for assignment, rebalance, and message consumption scenarios.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Implement optional HDFS Syncable writes",
      "activity_description": "Add an opt-in HDFS sink configuration, integrate synchronization operations into the file-writing and flush lifecycle, handle unsupported filesystem behavior and failures, preserve the existing default mode, and add unit and integration coverage.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Implement configurable HDFS in-use filename suffix",
      "activity_description": "Add configuration allowing the temporary inUseSuffix to be disabled or changed, update file creation, rollover, close, recovery, and rename handling, preserve the current default suffix, and add failure-recovery and compatibility tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Add Maven and Gradle custom-module upload targets",
      "activity_description": "Define Maven and Gradle tasks for packaging and uploading custom module fragments, connect them to the existing installation endpoint or repository flow, support credentials and configuration, provide useful failure handling, and test representative projects.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Add custom-module versioning support",
      "activity_description": "Extend module metadata, registration, lookup, deployment, and upgrade handling to support explicit versions, retain compatibility with existing modules, prevent ambiguous resolution, and add tests for installation, coexistence, selection, and upgrade scenarios.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Perform PHD 3.0 compatibility certification",
      "activity_description": "Set up or update the PHD 3.0 test environment, align dependencies and deployment configuration, execute smoke and representative integration tests, resolve compatibility defects, and record the supported certification matrix and known limitations.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature regression testing and release preparation",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete regression suite, add missing end-to-end scenarios across admin UI, Kafka, HDFS, and custom modules, review configuration backward compatibility, update user and developer documentation, prepare release notes, and perform final code cleanup.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 114
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Preserve backward compatibility by making all new configuration options optional and retaining existing defaults.
Implement explicit partition count as a source or stream configuration property, with validation against Kafka topic partition availability and clear startup errors.
Implement dynamic Kafka partition subscription using consumer assignment or subscription APIs so partition membership can change without requiring application redeployment.
Implement HDFS Syncable writes as an opt-in sink mode, invoking the appropriate filesystem synchronization operation and documenting its performance implications.
Implement the HDFS in-use suffix behavior as a configurable option; retain the existing temporary suffix as the default and allow an empty suffix to write directly to the configured filename.
Expose custom-module installation through Maven and Gradle tasks that invoke the existing module upload/install mechanism rather than duplicating repository logic.
Version custom modules using explicit module coordinates and version metadata, while retaining compatibility with existing unversioned module references.
Treat PHD 3.0 certification as a compatibility and integration-validation task covering supported Java, Hadoop, HDFS, Kafka, and deployment combinations.
Use automated unit, integration, regression, and command-line/UI-level tests where the existing project test infrastructure supports them.
assumptions: The increment is implemented in an existing Spring XD codebase with established build, test, module, Kafka, HDFS, and admin UI infrastructure.
The developer has access to the source repository, CI environment, Kafka and HDFS test environments, and a PHD 3.0 environment or equivalent certified distribution.
The reported admin UI job-creation failure is a defect in existing application behavior rather than a missing product capability, and no major redesign of authentication or authorization is required.
The exact desired routing semantics for explicit partition count are limited to configuring and validating the partition-related behavior; a new routing algorithm is not required.
Dynamic partition subscription does not require guaranteed exactly-once processing beyond the guarantees already provided by the existing Kafka source implementation.
HDFS Syncable support can be implemented using APIs available in the currently supported Hadoop dependency set.
Custom-module Maven and Gradle support means adding build targets and associated documentation, not creating new Maven or Gradle plugins.
Custom-module versioning applies to module packaging, registration, lookup, and deployment compatibility, without requiring a new enterprise artifact repository.
PHD 3.0 certification will identify and fix compatibility issues found in the supported test scenarios, but does not include certification of every Spring XD feature or deployment topology.
One workday represents one developer day of focused effort; elapsed calendar time, waiting for environments, and work by additional personnel are excluded.
Documentation and release notes are limited to the new configuration properties, commands, compatibility constraints, and upgrade guidance.
